The five included tests pass, but direct probes demonstrate unbounded batching memory and inconsistent quota validation at the reserve boundary. The referenced issue could not be retrieved, so specification coverage remains unverified.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Produce batches incrementally to bound memory usage — <worktree-b>/docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-uploader/uploader.py:13-14
  For large inputs, `list(records)` consumes the entire iterable, and the comprehension then retains every batch simultaneously. A tracemalloc probe with just one million integer records peaks at 48,228,640 bytes, already exceeding the documented 4 MB limit for ten million records. Yield batches incrementally instead of materializing both collections so large uploads do not require memory proportional to the entire input.

- [P2] Make quota boundary checks independent of floating-point rounding — <worktree-b>/docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-uploader/uploader.py:19-20
  At the reserve boundary, equivalent allocations receive different validation results: `[0.3, 0.3, 0.3]` succeeds, as the new test expects, while `[0.9]` and `[0.5, 0.4]` raise `ValueError`. Their computed reserves fall on opposite sides of `0.1` solely because of floating-point rounding. Define a consistent boundary policy using suitable precision or tolerance, and test equivalent splits alongside values genuinely above and below the floor.
